lines.caption: One, twelve, one hundred forty-four. Each number is twelve times the one before.

lines.text: How many three-number chains like this end at one hundred forty-four?
lines.caption: How many three-number chains like this end at one hundred forty-four?

lines.text: More than you'd think!
lines.caption: More than you'd think!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find every single one.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find every single one.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: How many increasing geometric sequences of three positive whole numbers, a, b, c,
lines.caption: How many increasing geometric sequences of three positive whole numbers, a, b, c,

lines.text: have c equal to one hundred forty-four?
lines.caption: have c equal to one hundred forty-four?

lines.text: Here are the five choices.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices.

lines.text: Geometric means we multiply by the same ratio each step, from a to b, then from b to c.
lines.caption: Geometric means we multiply by the same ratio each step, from a to b, then from b to c.

lines.text: Increasing means a is less than b, and b is less than c.
lines.caption: Increasing means a is less than b, and b is less than c.

lines.text: And watch out: the ratio doesn't have to be whole.
lines.caption: And watch out: the ratio doesn't have to be whole.

lines.text: Sixty-four, ninety-six, one hundred forty-four uses a ratio of three over two.
lines.caption: Sixty-four, ninety-six, one hundred forty-four uses a ratio of three over two.

lines.text: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's focus on the middle number, b.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's focus on the middle number, b.

lines.text: Same ratio means b over a equals c over b. So b times b equals a times c.
lines.caption: Same ratio means b over a equals c over b. So b times b equals a times c.

lines.text: With c equal to one hundred forty-four, a equals b squared,
lines.caption: With c equal to one hundred forty-four, a equals b squared,

lines.text: divided by one hundred forty-four.
lines.caption: divided by one hundred forty-four.

lines.text: Try a few. Six or eighteen give fractions. But twenty-four works: a is four.
lines.caption: Try a few. Six or eighteen give fractions. But twenty-four works: a is four.

lines.text: Here's the trick. One hundred forty-four is twelve squared.
lines.caption: Here's the trick. One hundred forty-four is twelve squared.

lines.text: So a is b over twelve, squared.
lines.caption: So a is b over twelve, squared.

lines.text: If b over twelve weren't whole, its square wouldn't be whole either.
lines.caption: If b over twelve weren't whole, its square wouldn't be whole either.

lines.text: Three over two squared is nine over four. Not whole!
lines.caption: Three over two squared is nine over four. Not whole!

lines.text: But a IS whole. So b over twelve must be whole.
lines.caption: But a IS whole. So b over twelve must be whole.

lines.text: Call it k. Then b is twelve k, and a is k squared.
lines.caption: Call it k. Then b is twelve k, and a is k squared.

lines.text: k equals one gives one, twelve, one hundred forty-four.
lines.caption: k equals one gives one, twelve, one hundred forty-four.

lines.text: k equals two gives four, twenty-four, one hundred forty-four. And so on.
lines.caption: k equals two gives four, twenty-four, one hundred forty-four. And so on.

lines.text: At k equals twelve, all three numbers are one hundred forty-four.
lines.caption: At k equals twelve, all three numbers are one hundred forty-four.

lines.text: That's not increasing, so we stop at eleven.
lines.caption: That's not increasing, so we stop at eleven.

lines.text: k can be one through eleven. That's eleven sequences, Choice C!
lines.caption: k can be one through eleven. That's eleven sequences, Choice C!

lines.text: Here's another way. Write the ratio as a fraction, p over q, in lowest terms.
lines.caption: Here's another way. Write the ratio as a fraction, p over q, in lowest terms.

lines.text: p is bigger than q, since the chain increases.
lines.caption: p is bigger than q, since the chain increases.

lines.text: Going backward from c, a is one hundred forty-four times q squared, over p squared.
lines.caption: Going backward from c, a is one hundred forty-four times q squared, over p squared.

lines.text: q squared shares no factor with p squared, so p squared must divide one hundred forty-four.
lines.caption: q squared shares no factor with p squared, so p squared must divide one hundred forty-four.

lines.text: The squares above one that divide it are four, nine, sixteen, thirty-six and one hundred forty-four.
lines.caption: The squares above one that divide it are four, nine, sixteen, thirty-six and one hundred forty-four.

lines.text: So p is two, three, four, six or twelve.
lines.caption: So p is two, three, four, six or twelve.

lines.text: That's one, plus two, plus two, plus two, plus four. Eleven again!
lines.caption: That's one, plus two, plus two, plus two, plus four. Eleven again!

lines.caption: Then b over six, squared, equals two times a. So two times a is a perfect square.

lines.text: In a geometric sequence, the middle times itself equals the outside two multiplied.
